About the Company
Rice University’s Department of Computer Science and Department of Materials Science and NanoEngineering are collaborating on READINESS, a new $20 million NSF-funded project focused on developing an AI-driven, remotely accessible autonomous laboratory. The project will connect four materials synthesis systems—CVD, thermal, PVD, and plasma CVD reactors—to support research involving 2D materials, oxides, and diamond films.
The READINESS facility will generate data from laboratory instruments, robotic systems, imaging equipment, spectra, and experimental workflows. The project aims to establish the data infrastructure needed to capture, organize, secure, and make this information accessible to researchers and collaborating teams.
About the Role
Rice University is seeking a Data Scientist to design, build, and operate the central data infrastructure for the READINESS project. This hands-on role combines data engineering, software development, storage infrastructure, and AI-enabled data retrieval. The successful candidate will take ownership of the central data lake, develop connections to laboratory instruments and robotic systems, and establish tools that allow researchers to query, analyze, and retrieve information from complex scientific datasets.
Reporting to the faculty leads of the READINESS Data Infrastructure working group, the Data Scientist will work closely with synthesis platform teams, robotics and AI/digital-twin groups, Rice IT and Information Security, and graduate and undergraduate students. A background in materials science, chemistry, or laboratory science is not required, as domain-specific knowledge can be developed through collaboration with scientific experts.
Key Responsibilities
Design, deploy, and operate the READINESS central data lake, including an S3-compatible object store hosted on Ceph or in the cloud, with appropriate bucket structures, versioning, and access policies.
Develop and maintain ingestion connectors that collect data from synthesis tools, characterization instruments, and robotic systems, including structured, de-identified metadata and provenance links.
Design and maintain metadata and provenance schemas, along with a Python client library for project teams to read and write data.
Deploy and administer the SQL query layer using Trino and Hive Metastore over Parquet, as well as APIs for researchers, the user portal, digital-twin teams, and AI applications.
Build embedding pipelines and GPU-resident vector indexes for images, spectra, and logs, supporting similarity search and retrieval-augmented generation.
Develop and demonstrate AI agents that answer questions about experiments by retrieving relevant information from the data lake in collaboration with the AI and Digital Twins working group.
Implement and maintain security controls, including Rice single sign-on with multi-factor authentication, role-based access, encryption, and immutable audit logging.
Work with Rice Information Security and Research Security on system design reviews and compliance requirements.
Monitor system health, conduct data integrity checks, maintain backups, and document and test recovery procedures.
Gather requirements from synthesis, characterization, and robotics teams, participate in working-group meetings, and establish standards for data formats, metadata, and access.
Prepare technical documentation, user guides, and onboarding materials, and train researchers and partner-site collaborators to use the data infrastructure.
Mentor graduate and undergraduate students working on data infrastructure projects.
Perform other related duties as assigned.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, data science, engineering, or a related quantitative field.
At least three years of professional experience in data engineering, data science, software engineering, research computing, or a related area.
Strong programming skills, including the ability to write production-quality, tested, and documented code.
Proficiency in SQL and relational data modeling, including scientific or operational database schemas.
Experience with object storage such as S3, Ceph, or MinIO; columnar formats such as Parquet; and distributed query engines such as Trino, Presto, Spark, or similar tools.
Working knowledge of Linux administration, Docker or Kubernetes, and at least one major cloud platform, such as AWS or Azure.
Familiarity with PyTorch, embedding models, vector databases, and retrieval-augmented or agentic LLM applications.
Understanding of authentication and access controls, including SSO, SAML, OIDC, role-based access, and audit logging, as well as secure research-data handling.
Ability to connect software with physical instruments and devices through network-based or file-based protocols.
Ability to learn unfamiliar scientific domains, translate collaborator requirements into working systems, manage competing requests, and communicate clearly across technical disciplines.
Preferred Qualifications
Five or more years of professional experience building and operating data systems.
Experience developing data pipelines for scientific instruments, laboratory automation, manufacturing, or IoT and telemetry systems.
Experience operating Ceph or comparable software-defined storage, or managing cloud object-storage environments at a scale of 100 TB or more.
Experience with GPU-accelerated similarity search tools such as FAISS, Milvus, or Qdrant, and serving open-weight large language models.
Experience in academic research or national laboratories, including collaboration with institutional IT and security teams.
Experience monitoring production data systems and implementing backup and recovery procedures.
Experience with ROS or rosbag is a plus.
Salary & Benefits
The hiring range is up to $105,000 annually. This is a one-year, term-limited, benefits-eligible position funded through a grant, soft funds, and/or restricted funds. Renewal may be possible dependin

About the Company
The company builds infrastructure for collecting, processing, and organizing large volumes of public web data used by companies developing advanced AI models. Its technology supports Grass, a bandwidth-sharing network that enables a distributed web crawler, along with data pipelines for ingesting, segmenting, and annotating billions of videos, transcripts, and audio files. The team focuses on expanding access to high-quality web data for AI development through scalable technical infrastructure.
About the Role
The role focuses on building and maintaining the data infrastructure required to collect, process, and deliver large-scale web datasets. You will work across Python development, web scraping, distributed data pipelines, data warehousing, and infrastructure management to support reliable data access and processing.
This position suits an experienced engineer who can write production-grade Python code, manage high-volume scraping workflows, and operate distributed systems across multiple workers and servers. You will also contribute to database optimization, pipeline troubleshooting, technical documentation, and research and development initiatives that improve the company's data products.
Key Responsibilities
Maintain, optimize, and troubleshoot database queries and data systems to improve data access, processing efficiency, and reliability.
Develop and maintain scalable data pipelines for collecting, processing, transforming, validating, and delivering large datasets.
Build, test, and maintain web scraping scripts and tools for collecting publicly available data in accordance with company requirements.
Work with distributed data collection and processing workloads across multiple workers and servers.
Develop and maintain workflows for ingesting, segmenting, and annotating large volumes of video, transcript, and audio data.
Monitor pipeline performance, investigate data quality issues, and implement fixes to maintain accuracy and operational continuity.
Document database queries, pipeline processes, scraping workflows, technical decisions, issues, and resolutions.
Participate in research and development projects focused on improving data products and engineering workflows.
Support containerized workloads, deployments, and scaling of scraping and data processing systems.
Develop and maintain scalable APIs and contribute to CI/CD workflows for data engineering operations.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.
Advanced Python programming skills, including asynchronous programming, multiprocessing, and production-grade code for long-running data jobs.
Hands-on experience with high-volume web scraping, including proxies, rate limiting, and anti-bot evasion techniques.
Experience designing and operating distributed data pipelines using task queues such as Celery, Kafka, RabbitMQ, or similar technologies.
Practical experience with columnar or analytical data warehouses, including complex analytical queries, partitioning strategies, and cost-aware cloud querying.
Experience with Docker and Kubernetes, including containerizing workloads and managing deployments.
Comfort managing Linux servers and troubleshooting performance issues involving disk I/O, networking, and memory.
Experience with CI/CD for data workflows using tools such as GitHub Actions or ArgoCD.
Experience writing scalable APIs.
Ability to troubleshoot data systems, maintain data quality, and document technical work.
Preferred Qualifications / Requirements
Experience with Databend, ClickHouse, or BigQuery is strongly preferred.
Experience with platform APIs and large media or metadata datasets, including data from video platforms and social media.
Experience creating Helm charts and Kubernetes manifests, as well as managing autoscaling for scraping and processing workloads.
Location and Work Arrangement
The company operates as a fully remote team.
Salary & Benefits
The company offers a competitive salary, benefits, and equity package. Specific compensation figures and individual benefit details are not provided in the listing.

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44782.description_preview:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.
About The Role:
As our new software engineer in CrowdStrike, you’ll contribute to the LogScale application for observability, log management, and security events. As a member of the new US based engine team you will focus on the LogScale engine that makes LogScale scale by developing new features as well as improving existing functionality. This is a highly distributed system that ingests
Petabytes
of data per day through both our SaaS and On Premise offerings. You will be joining a distributed team of highly collaborative engineers who share a strong passion for the product. In this role you will get a chance to work on hard engineering problems that do not have well-defined solutions. You will become one of the go-to experts of the LogScale engine, and will have a broad understanding of the entire LogScale architecture.
Teams in LogScale have a great amount of autonomy, and own a part of the LogScale experience, from ideation and development to deployment and feedback. This includes ensuring high quality of the features they deliver, by writing automated tests, and performing manual tests. Moreover, we do not just throw over features to our operations teams, but we constantly observe and monitor new features in production, with LogScale dashboards of course.
An important part of our work is making sure that LogScale continues to be scalable in terms of efficiently ingesting and digesting events, querying for the right data, while also ensuring the stability of the clusters. Some of the critical elements that the team is working on improving is the query execution engine that makes the LogScale queries be lightning fast. The team is also working with our internal “global” data storage using Kafka and the storage engine that ensures data is stored in the right number of replicas as well as on the correct nodes and in bucket storage such as S3. You will be playing a crucial role in ensuring that LogScale can continue with its successful durability and high availability.
This role is hybrid, requiring 2-3 days per week on-site at one of the posted locations.
What You'll Do:
Work in a team of friendly, trustworthy and knowledgeable colleagues
Work on cross-team platform-level initiatives and projects
Participate in scoping, designing and developing of new features and lead delivery of solutions to open-ended problems
Contribute to moving the scalability of our LogScale engine to the next level
Develop the LogScale backend in Scala and extending our engine to keep LogScale scale with increasing ingest load while ensuring high availability
Communicate technical decisions through design documents, technical talks and improving our internal documentation.

Research Engineer - Post-Training & Small Language Models (SLMs), Healthcare AI
Three hundred fifty million Americans rely on a healthcare system whose decision-making has become slow, costly, and adversarial - care delayed by prior authorization and paperwork, claims that misfire, clinical decisions made without the right information at the right moment, and patients who struggle to navigate or afford the care they need. Deloitte has a new AI-first effort,, backed by $1B in committed investment, building the reasoning models and agentic systems to rebuild how that system decides - across payers, providers, and life sciences, and for the patients they serve - so that care is faster, fairer, and far less wasteful. This is not AI applied at the margins. It is a ground-up rebuild of the decision-making machinery behind American healthcare, at national scale.
This is resourced to do real post-training at scale - committed investment in GPU compute and training infrastructure, not toy fine-tunes.
As a Research Engineer on our post-training team, you will design, train, evaluate, and align the models that reason about healthcare - working across the full post-training lifecycle to shape model behavior for clinical and operational decisioning across the industry. Healthcare decisioning is one of the cleanest verifiable-reward domains outside math and code: the problems are hard. We ground that reward in real signals - clinical policy and criteria, adjudicated outcomes, and clinical-expert judgment - so correctness is checkable rather than asserted.
You will own the post-training stack for our clinical reasoning models end to end - from data and reward design through trained, evaluated models that ship. This is not a prompt-engineering role. We are looking for people who understand not just how to use LLMs, but how to improve and shape model behavior through advanced post-training.
You do not need a healthcare background. We pair every engineer with clinical and domain experts and teach you the domain - you bring the modeling depth.
We hire on demonstrated depth, not years - the level you join at is determined through our interview process, based on the depth and judgment you demonstrate, not your years in a title.
Work you'll do
Post-training & alignment
Design and execute post-training pipelines: supervised fine-tuning (SFT), preference optimization, and reinforcement learning / alignment workflows.
Build and optimize training using techniques such as SFT, RLHF, PPO, DPO, GRPO, RLAIF, and Constitutional AI, and understand how each affects reasoning quality, safety, latency, cost, and reliability.
Train reasoning models for healthcare decisioning using verifiable-reward RL - designing reward signals and verifiers grounded in clinical guidelines, policy and criteria, and adjudicated outcomes.
Reward modeling & data
Develop reward models and preference datasets to improve reasoning quality, factuality, safety, policy adherence, and task performance.
Curate, clean, synthesize, and evaluate large-scale instruction, preference, and domain-specific datasets, with rigorous filtering, deduplication, and quality control.
Build verification and reward pipelines from our proprietary clinical, claims, and operational data and from clinical-expert labeling - turning guidelines, policy, and adjudicated outcomes into checkable reward signals at scale.
Efficient fine-tuning, training & inference infrastructure
Implement efficient fine-tuning strategies including LoRA, QLoRA, PEFT, and adapter-based approaches; build scalable distributed training using DeepSpeed, FSDP, Megatron-LM, Ray, or equivalent.
Optimize inference performance - latency, throughput, quantization, and deployment efficiency - for production, including frameworks such as vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, or TGI.
Small language models & open-weight models
Train and optimize open-weight models such as Llama, Qwen, Mistral, or DeepSeek; build specialized small language models (SLMs) for on-premise and cloud-hybrid deployment with strong performance-per-dollar.
Evaluation, safety & red teaming
Design evaluation frameworks covering reasoning, hallucination detection, factuality, instruction following, structured outputs, and domain-specific metrics.
Build healthcare-grade evaluation - held-out clinical benchmarks, deployment regression gates, calibration and uncertainty, factuality against ground truth, and bias/fairness evaluation across patient populations and subgroups - co-designed with clinical experts.
Apply PHI/HIPAA-aware data handling and produce model documentation suitable for regulated clinical use.
Perform red teaming and adversarial testing to identify alignment failures, unsafe behaviors, jailbreak vulnerabilities, and regression risks; collaborate with agentic and application teams to improve tool use, grounding, and long-horizon reasoning.

The work spans the healthcare industry - payers, providers, and life sciences - and involves genuinely hard reasoning problems, nuanced operational workflows, and a high bar for reliability, with little tolerance for shallow or unreliable outputs. We pair frontier AI research with production-grade engineering, and we ship into real clinical and operational settings rather than leaving models in the lab.
You can go deep. The team sub-specializes across post-training research, data and reward engineering, and training and inference infrastructure - you won't be expected to own all of it alone.

Altamira Technologies
has a long and successful history providing innovative solutions throughout the U.S. National Security community. Headquartered in McLean, Virginia, Altamira serves the defense, intelligence and homeland security communities by focusing on creating innovative solutions leveraging common standards in architecture, data and security. Altamira believes that our people and the culture of our company differentiate us from other companies.
We focus on recruiting talented, self-motivated employees that strive to grow and improve their work. Join our team of experts as we engineer national security!
Altamira is seeking a Research and Development Engineer to support the National Space Intelligence Center (NSIC) in advancing its critical mission. In this role, you will research, develop, and prototype software capabilities focused on space-based object visualization and data exploitation. Your work will involve algorithm development and AI/ML experimentation while utilizing disciplined engineering practices to transform research objectives into practical, scalable capabilities. The ideal candidate has a proven track record of developing software to solve complex technical problems, evaluating potential solutions, and effectively communicating results. Experience in R&D, algorithm development, or applied AI/ML is highly preferred.
Responsibilities
Research and Prototyping: Research concepts, evaluate algorithms, and develop software prototypes to explore technical approaches and demonstrate potential capabilities.
AI/ML Development: Train, evaluate, and tune AI/ML models to improve data exploitation, object characterization, and visualization capabilities.
Workflow Development: Identify operational workflows, define technical requirements, and break down research objectives into achievable tasks and deliverables.
Technical Documentation and Communication: Document approaches, experiments, results, and recommendations while providing regular progress updates and communicating risks or blockers.
Agile Execution: Participate in Scrum ceremonies, estimate and scope work, track progress, and deliver incremental results aligned with sprint objectives.
Collaboration and Mentorship: Collaborate across technical disciplines, contribute to code reviews, share knowledge, and mentor junior engineers in software development and research practices.
Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Mathematics, Physics, or a related technical field from an accredited college or university.
Proficiency using programming languages such as Python, Rust, Go, and/or C/C++, with working knowledge of algorithms, data structures, software design, and automated testing.
Familiarity with machine learning fundamentals, including model training, validation, and performance evaluation.
Ability to independently investigate technical problems, evaluate alternative approaches, and develop prototypes to test hypotheses.
Ability to scope and estimate work, document findings, communicate progress and blockers, and collaborate effectively within an Agile Scrum team.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to share technical knowledge and support the development of junior engineers.
At least 2 years of professional experience performing research and development, data science, or software engineering.
Able to obtain a TS/SCI Clearance

About Wonder
Everything’s on the menu at Wonder. Except compromise.
Wonder is the mealtime platform built to feed every craving in one order. With Wonder, you can mix and match hundreds of dishes from 20+ exclusive restaurants in a single order, so everyone gets exactly what they’re craving. Enjoy everything from tacos to Thai with $0 delivery fees, plus dine-in or pick up at a Wonder location near you. Each dish is made to order on-site by our culinary team and served hot.
Behind the scenes, Wonder owns and operates every step of the dining experience, from recipe development to the technology that powers our experience, allowing us to deliver quality, variety, and consistency at scale.
Join us as we work to make great food more accessible.
The Impact You Will Make
Develop, test, and deploy SuiteScript 2.x customizations, including suitelets, user event scripts, scheduled scripts, map/reduce scripts, RESTlets, and workflow action scripts, to support financial workflows and automation.
Configure and maintain NetSuite environments across multiple subsidiaries, including custom records, saved searches, workflows, roles, and permissions.
Support ERP migration projects (D365 to NetSuite, NetSuite to NetSuite) by performing data loading, validation, entity setup, and cutover activities.
Build and maintain integrations between NetSuite and adjacent financial systems, including our homegrown Accounting Gateway (ACG), FloQast, Anaplan, BigQuery/Airflow, Ignite, and Adaptive, plus SFTP data feeds, using REST/SOAP APIs and middleware patterns.
Write and troubleshoot SQL-based queries and saved searches to support reporting, reconciliation, and data validation needs.
Address the growing backlog of Financial Systems support tickets, resolving configuration issues, report requests, and user access questions to reduce dependency on senior technical resources.
Build and execute test plans for releases across NetSuite and, as scope expands, Anaplan, Floqast, and ZipHQ.
Document technical designs, configurations, and runbooks to reduce single-person dependency on senior team members and support institutional knowledge retention.
Collaborate with third-party implementation partners (LIDD) to execute project deliverables and ensure quality of configuration and development work.
Contribute to IPO readiness efforts by supporting chart of accounts standardization, bank reconciliation automation, fixed asset module configuration, and financial reporting infrastructure.
Assist in developing a repeatable playbook for integrating future acquisitions into the NetSuite platform.
What You Bring To The Table
1–3 years of hands-on experience with Oracle NetSuite, including configuration and administration.
Working knowledge of JavaScript and SuiteScript (1.0 and/or 2.x), including user event scripts, suitelets, scheduled scripts, RESTlets, and workflow action scripts, or demonstrated ability to learn quickly with mentorship.
Foundational understanding of object-oriented programming concepts and NetSuite's underlying data model, including best practices for querying and reporting.
Experience with NetSuite data migration (CSV imports, data validation, entity setup).
Familiarity with NetSuite financial modules: General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Fixed Assets, and Bank Reconciliation.
Exposure to system integration patterns (REST/SOAP APIs, SFTP, middleware) and data formats (SQL, XML, JSON) is a plus.
Experience working in a multi-entity or multi-subsidiary NetSuite environment preferred.
NetSuite certifications (e.g., SuiteFoundation, SuiteCloud Developer) are a plus but not required.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
Ability to work cross-functionally with Finance, Accounting, and Technology stakeholders, and to communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Accounting, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Chicago: $92,000- $122,000
Wonder uses geographic-specific salary structures, which means the salary offered may vary depending on where the job is located. The final salary offer will take into account various factors, such as the candidate's skills, education, training, credentials, and experience.
Benefits
The benefits applicable to this role include a competitive compensation package with equity and a 401(k). We also offer a choice of medical, dental, and vision plans, company paid short and long term disability coverage, paid time off including flexible time off for exempt employees, paid vacation for non-exempt employees, and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable law in addition to paid parental leave, discounted meals and exclusive perks across the Wonder family of brands.
Eligibility, effective dates, and available plan options vary by employment classification and location. To learn more about benefits for this role, visit our Careers page here.

Project Description
Hiredbuddy is seeking an entry-level Full Stack Developer to join our remote team. You'll build and maintain web applications, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and grow your skills in a supportive environment. If you're passionate about coding and ready to make an impact, apply today!
Full Description
As an Entry Level Full Stack Developer at Hiredbuddy, you will be an integral part of our engineering team, contributing to the design, development, and maintenance of web applications that serve a diverse client base. This remote role is perfect for someone who is eager to apply foundational coding skills in a real-world environment while learning from experienced professionals. You will work on both front-end and back-end components, ensuring seamless user experiences and robust server-side logic.
Key Responsibilities
Develop and maintain responsive web applications using modern JavaScript frameworks such as React or Vue.js for the front end.
Build and integrate RESTful APIs and microservices using Node.js, Express, or similar back-end technologies.
Write clean, maintainable, and well-documented code that follows industry best practices.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams including designers, product managers, and other developers to deliver high-quality features.
Participate in code reviews, provide constructive feedback, and continuously improve development processes.
Troubleshoot and debug applications to optimize performance and ensure reliability.
Work with databases (SQL or NoSQL) to design schemas, write queries, and manage data storage.
Use version control systems like Git for collaborative development and deployment.
Stay updated with emerging technologies and suggest improvements to existing systems.
Assist in testing and deployment using CI/CD pipelines and cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, or Heroku).
Technologies and Tools
Our stack evolves, but currently we rely on:
Front-end: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), React, Redux, or Vue.js
Back-end: Node.js, Express, Python (Django/Flask) or Ruby on Rails
Databases: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or MySQL
Version Control: Git, GitHub/GitLab
Deployment: Docker, AWS, Netlify, Vercel
Testing: Jest, Mocha, Chai, Cypress
Communication: Slack, Zoom, Jira, Trello
Growth and Development
At Hiredbuddy, we invest in our team's growth. You will receive direct mentorship from senior engineers, regular feedback, and access to resources that help you advance your skills. We encourage exploration of new tools and technologies, and we provide a clear path for progression to mid-level and senior roles. Your contributions will directly impact the success of our products and the satisfaction of our clients.
Work Environment
This is a fully remote position, allowing you to work from anywhere within the United States. We value work-life balance and flexibility, while maintaining a strong sense of community through virtual events, pair programming sessions, and open communication channels. You will have the support you need to succeed, whether it's through structured onboarding, regular check-ins, or a dedicated buddy system.
If you are ready to launch your career as a Full Stack Developer and make a meaningful impact, we would love to hear from you.
Requirements
0-2 years of experience in full stack development (internships and personal projects count)
Proficiency in at least one front-end framework (React, Vue, or Angular) and one back-end language (Node.js, Python, or Ruby)
Understanding of RESTful APIs and HTTP fundamentals
Familiarity with relational and/or NoSQL databases
Knowledge of version control systems (Git)
Ability to write clean, testable code
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
Excellent communication and teamwork abilities
Self-motivated and able to work independently in a remote environment
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
Benefits
Competitive entry-level salary with performance reviews
100% remote work flexibility
Health, dental, and vision insurance
Paid time off and public holidays
Home office stipend
Access to learning platforms and certification courses
Mentorship from senior developers
Opportunity for career growth and role advancement

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
About The Team
The Sentry Tower Software team is responsible for developing robotic systems that provide force protection capabilities, monitoring the perimeter of secure areas, land or sea, for approaching people, vehicles, and vessels. We live in a world where security officers are increasingly overwhelmed by sensor data feeds. Our products leverage advanced sensor fusion and autonomy to seamlessly render activity in the environment to Lattice’s common operating picture.
About The Job
We are looking for a Software Engineer with a focus in Manufacturing to join our rapidly growing team in Costa Mesa. In this role you will be responsible for building and maintaining software for current and next generation Sentry Tower systems. You will be responsible for developing automated test suites and user-friendly interfaces to streamline hardware verification and issue diagnosis for non-technical users. You will implement robust error-capturing mechanisms that provide actionable insights for efficient troubleshooting and quality assurance.
Every tower we ship passes through this software. It is what proves a unit works before it leaves the floor, which makes it the last chance to catch a defect while the hardware is still in reach and the fix costs an hour instead of a trip to a site. A test that passes when it should not have is the most expensive kind of bug we have, because it ships.
The honest version: your users are technicians on a production floor, not engineers, and their time is the constraint. Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About The Team
As part of the Enterprise Product team, the Enterprise Engineering team is responsible for bridging the gap between Stripe's core capabilities and the bespoke needs of the world's largest organizations. Our mission is to improve Stripe's product-market fit with enterprise users to win more deals and grow revenue, while giving every enterprise user an excellent experience as they onboard, activate, and grow their business with Stripe.
Enterprise Engineering tackles ambiguous, complex problems in a cross functional manner to deliver an exceptional Enterprise experience on Stripe. The key missions of the team is to 1) develop specialized Enterprise-grade product features for industry verticals 2) provide a configuration platform that streamlines onboarding Enterprise users onto Stripe and 3) deliver a consistently great and smooth experience when migrating sensitive data onto Stripe.
The team consists of full stack engineers who tackle this user goal through scalable and secure infrastructure, dashboard interfaces and internal administrative tools.
What you’ll do
Responsibilities
Design, build, and maintain scalable, reliable and performant services and systems
Collaborate with other engineers across Stripe, as well as stakeholders across product, design, risk, legal, and operations
Build easy to use systems that streamlines adoption of Stripe and enable safe migration of data
Make effective tradeoffs that consider business priorities, user experience, and a sustainable technical foundation
Improve engineering standards, tooling, and processes
Who you are
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum Requirements
2+ years of industry experience shipping high-quality products
Strong analytical capability and ability to quickly ramp up in a new area, and tackle ambiguous problems
Enjoy and have experience building end-to-end solution, including full development lifecycle of deploying and maintaining this infrastructure
Experience with web software development
Hold yourself and others to a high bar when working with production systems
Take pride in taking ownership and driving projects to business impact
Preferred Qualifications
Strong collaboration and communication skills with both technical and non-technical counterparts
Able to reason clearly and move with urgency in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment
Able to think outside of the box and be creative in designing and delivering the best solutions for our users
Enjoy a range of product development activities, from architecture design and planning, to user interviews, to writing code
In-office expectations
Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.
Pay and benefits
The annual US base salary range for this role is $190,400 - $285,600. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.
Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44730.description_preview:
Job Summary
The AI Platform team is building the shared runtime that every AI agent at MeridianLink will run on as part of the MeridianLink One platform: model gateway, orchestration, memory, and observability, delivered as reusable services so product teams build agents once and run them safely for hundreds of credit union and lender customers. This role builds the trust and explainability layer of that runtime: the tracing, evaluation, and explanation capabilities that let engineers understand exactly what a multi-agent workflow did and why, and that let product teams show end customers the right level of explanation to trust an agent's output.
This role has a strong dotted-line relationship to MeridianLink's Security Operations team, so the platform's trust guarantees and Security's threat models are built from the same picture.
About The Opportunity
This is a deeply technical, hands-on engineering role and an integral part of the platform itself. You will write the code that traces agent actions across a multi-agent workflow, adopt and extend leading open-source explainability and observability frameworks, and build the primitives product teams use to surface explanations to lenders, credit unions, and their borrowers. You should have real hands-on experience with LLM-based systems and a strong pull toward the problems of trust, tracing, and evaluation. You do not need to be an expert in all of it. This is a place to build that expertise while the platform is being built, working alongside a Staff engineer team lead and architects who will invest in your growth.
What it means to be an L2 AI Engineer at MeridianLink
L2 AI Engineers handle a broad range of work independently, from bug fixes to feature development. They have developed a specialization and are deepening it. They write code that other engineers trust, ask good questions, and are starting to help the engineers around them. L2 AI Engineers at MeridianLink are active, daily users of AI-assisted development tools.
Technical Execution & Delivery
Completes assigned features and bug fixes independently, with limited need for day-to-day guidance
Designs components within a well-defined scope; escalates questions on complex system design rather than guessing
Participates in code review and provides constructive feedback
Surfaces blockers proactively rather than waiting for check-ins
Craft & Professionalism
Writes tests that cover the functionality they ship
Monitors and responds to issues with their own work
Documents decisions and implementation details that others will need later
Agent Tracing & Explainability
Understands how to instrument an agent so a single conversation can be followed from the first user message through every model call, tool call, retrieval, agent handoff, and decision to the final response
Builds the correlation that ties actions across multiple agents in one workflow into a single readable trace
Turns raw trace data into an explanation a human can follow: what the agent did, what it relied on, and why it chose that path
Customer-Facing Trust & Explanation
Understands that the explanation an engineer needs and the explanation a borrower or loan officer needs are different, and builds for both
Works with product engineers on what an agent should disclose at the product surface: what it did, what data it used, how confident it was, and what a human should verify
Applies judgment about the right level of explanation for a regulated lending and account-opening context
Trust & Explainability Frameworks
Familiar with the open-source landscape for LLM observability, tracing, and evaluation, and can evaluate a framework against the platform's needs
Integrates and extends existing frameworks rather than rebuilding them, and builds what does not exist yet
Keeps the platform's instrumentation aligned to emerging standards so traces stay portable across tools
Agent Evaluation & Quality
Understands how to measure the quality of non-deterministic output: golden datasets, rubric and LLM-as-judge scoring, and regression baselines
Builds evaluation checks that run in CI so a model swap, prompt change, or tool change is tested before it reaches customers

Your opportunity
New Relic's whole platform runs on an assumption: by the time a request reaches any service, someone has already answered two questions, who is this, and what are they allowed to do. The Access & Governance Platform team builds and runs the systems that answer both. On the authentication side, that means login, session and token management, and enterprise SSO integrations (SAML, OIDC, OAuth2) for customers who need to plug New Relic into their own identity provider. Because these services sit underneath everything else, the problems here are rarely simple CRUD. You're modeling access at the scale of every account and organization on the platform, keeping login working through traffic spikes and identity-provider outages, and building the self-service tooling other engineering teams use to adopt fine-grained authorization for their own services. You'll also carry on-call for these systems, because when they have a bad day, so does the rest of New Relic.

Company Overview
Function Health is the AI operating system for health, designed to empower people to live 100 healthy years. We are redefining how individuals understand, measure, and improve their health by moving beyond the limitations of traditional care and enabling comprehensive, continuous insight into human biology. Function has been recognized as one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies of 2024, and is venture-backed by Redpoint and other leading venture firms. Over half a million members have joined Function to take control of their health.
Through comprehensive lab testing, MRI and CT imaging, longitudinal data, and guidance from AI and clinical teams, Function gives members a complete and continuous view of their health, and the clarity to act on it. Through acquisitions across imaging, mobile phlebotomy, and supplement tracking and optimization, Function is building an integrated health platform that spans the full path from testing to health clarity to daily action.
Function recently announced a $298M Series B and is entering its next chapter of growth. We are growing our team and seeking talent that deeply believes in our mission to positively impact global health, has a relentless bias toward action, and a growth mindset. Function fosters a collaborative and dynamic environment where every day we build the future.
Role
We are seeking a curious, motivated Associate Software Engineer to join our engineering team at Function. You will help design, build, and ship software that gives our members access to their health data in real time. Function is a highly AI-native engineering environment: our engineers use AI tools every day to write, review, test, and debug code, and to move faster without lowering the bar on quality. You'll work closely with experienced engineers who will mentor you, review your code, and help you grow quickly, while you take on real, meaningful work from your first weeks.
The ideal candidate is early in their engineering career, detail-oriented, eager to learn, and energized by a fast-paced environment. You are comfortable working with a variety of AI engineering workflows and see AI as a way to multiply your impact. This role is a great fit for someone who wants to build strong engineering fundamentals while contributing to a mission that matters.
Key Responsibilities
As an Associate Software Engineer at Function, you will:
AI-Native Software Development: Write clean, well-tested, maintainable code for well-scoped features and bug fixes, using AI coding assistants and agentic workflows as part of your daily process. Learn our codebase and engineering standards, and contribute to scalable, secure systems under the guidance of senior engineers.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with teammates across engineering, product, design, and clinical teams to understand requirements, ask clarifying questions, and communicate progress and blockers clearly.
Project Delivery: Own small to medium-sized tasks from start to finish, including planning, implementation, testing, code review, and deployment. Contribute to team projects that support Function's strategic goals.
Technical Problem Solving: Debug and resolve technical issues with support from your team. Break down problems into manageable pieces, and learn to investigate root causes using logs, monitoring, testing, and AI-assisted analysis.
Quality and Engineering Practices: Participate in code reviews, write unit and integration tests, and follow our CI/CD, Agile, and documentation practices. Critically review AI-generated code for correctness, security, and maintainability before it ships, and take ownership of everything you commit. Help keep our data accurate and our systems reliable.
AI Workflow Fluency: Learn and share effective ways of working with AI, such as prompting, providing context, using coding agents, and automating repetitive tasks. Help the team improve how we build with AI.
Learning and Growth: Stay curious about new technologies and approaches. Seek feedback, take on stretch work, and apply what you learn to improve our platform.
Required

Experience: 1-2 years of professional software engineering experience (internships and co-ops included)
Education: Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Artificial Intelligence or Applied Mathematics.
Programming Fundamentals: Working proficiency in Python (or a comparable language such as Java, TypeScript, or Go), plus a solid grasp of data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented design. You understand the code you ship, whether you or an AI wrote it.
AI-Native Mindset: Comfort working with a variety of AI engineering workflows, such as AI coding assistants, agentic tools, and LLM-assisted debugging, testing, and code review. You know how to get good results from these tools and how to verify their output.
Engineering Basics: Familiarity with version control (Git), testing practices, and APIs and web services.
Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills and a knack for breaking down unfamiliar problems.
Communication and Collaboration: Clear written and verbal communication, and comfort working in a remote, distributed team.
Commitment to Learning: A growth mindset. You welcome feedback, ask good questions, and question assumptions, including the AI's.
Mission Alignment: Interest in using technology to improve healthcare and help people manage their health.

Exposure to cloud platforms (AWS or Google Cloud) and containerization (Docker).
Familiarity with Agile methodologies, test-driven development, or CI/CD pipelines.
Experience with SQL or relational databases.
Prior internship or project experience in healthcare, health data, or a startup environment.

About Us
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
The Job
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
About You
You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.
You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.
You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.
Nice to have:
Developer-facing products, protocol or gateway work, or infrastructure at scale.
Background in security, identity, or permission systems.
Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.
Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.
What we offer:
Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.
Unusual scope and ownership of features that ship to enterprise customers.
Building and deploying agents on the same platform we sell.
Direct access to the founders, customer context, and product direction, with mentorship as you grow.
Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

At
ABB
, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.
This position reports to:
IS Manager
__
As an intern, you will have the opportunity to gain practical experience through various projects. Each day, you will acquire knowledge by performing tasks as directed. You will also showcase your skills by supporting ABB’s operations and enhancing personal education/employment opportunities.
The work model for the role is onsite/hybrid in Cary, NC.
You will be mainly accountable for:
The agents and connectors: building the AI layer's agents, tools and data connectors in Python, reading from our business systems through APIs and SQL.
Multi-step workflows: designing agent flows in LangGraph or a comparable framework, with human approval built in. You'll work with read-only access and sandbox environments; nothing writes to a live system without human approval.
The right retrieval for each question: a database query, an API call or a document search, and knowing which one fits.
Evaluation: building evaluation sets, measuring whether answers are right, and improving them.
Weekly delivery: shipping small pieces every week and demoing them to the team and to business users.
AI assistants, owned: using AI coding assistants openly, and being able to explain every line you commit.
Documentation: writing up what you build and learn so the next person can pick it up.
Qualifications for the role:
Currently enrolled in a master's program, or in the third or fourth year of a bachelor's program, in computer science, mathematics, data science or industrial engineering in the United States. Master's students preferred.
Available to continue part-time, remotely, for about six months after the summer, alongside your studies.
Intern must have reliable transportation to and from the worksite during the summer.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without company sponsorship now and in the future.
Python you've shipped: a project someone else can run, with git and tests. Include a link with your application.
Hands-on experience building with LLMs: model APIs, tool calling, structured outputs.
SQL, including joins across multiple tables.
A working understanding of REST APIs and JSON.
Valued, not required:
LangGraph or another agent framework; embeddings, vector search and RAG; MCP; knowledge graphs (for example Neo4j); a cloud platform; any exposure to supply chain, manufacturing or ERP concepts.
Why ABB?
What's in it for you
We want you to bring your full self to work—your ideas, your energy, your ambition. You’ll have the tools and freedom to grow your skills, shape your path, and take on challenges that matter. Here, your work creates impact you can see and feel, every day.

FlexTrade Systems is a provider of customized multi-asset execution and order management trading solutions for buy- and sell-side financial institutions. Through deep client partnerships with some of the world's largest, most complex and demanding capital markets firms, we develop flexible tools, technology and innovation that deliver our clients a competitive edge. Our globally distributed engineering teams focus on adaptable technology and open architecture to develop highly sophisticated trading solutions that can automate and scale with your business strategies.
At FlexTrade, we hold our values close to heart, with pride and gratitude, as they guide us in everything that we do. We are dedicated to giving our clients a competitive edge, taking ownership of our responsibilities, being flexible to adapt to ever changing environment and technology, bringing integrity to every interaction and we continue to improve, grow together and collaborate as one team. All of these while having fun truly makes FlexTrade a wonderful place to work
.
The Team
We are looking for a mid-level, skilled C++ developer to join our team. The ideal candidate will have experience working with low-latency products and trading workflows. The successful candidate will be passionate about finance and technology. You approach problems not only from a technical point of view, but also from the business aspect. As a C++ developer, you will be responsible for designing, building, and maintaining a critical component in the middle office system and integrate with counterparties with this system. You will also be responsible for delivering continuous optimization for latency, scale, and resiliency improvements. We use agile scrum methodology to plan and manage our projects. We believe a great developer will pick up skills as needed.

You will be part of a small close-knit team of engineers that work in an Agile and collaborative fashion to build performant software that sits at the core of FlexTrade's business. Working in close collaboration with client-facing teams, you will design and develop solutions for middle office enhancements & issues and assist teams in rollout to production.
Responsibilities
C++ Development: Enhance and improve the middle office system
C++ Development: Integrate with third parties to the middle office system
Take ownership of specific modules within the system and work on bug fixes and enhancements.
Bachelors or Master’s Degree in Computer Science (or related field).
Minimum 3-4 years of professional software development experience using C++.
Proficient in C++ (Concurrent programming techniques: Shared memory, Atomics and lock-free data structures)
Strong understanding of data structures, algorithms, and software design principles.
Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.
Working knowledge of Linux C++ development environment: vim, gdb, make, valgrind etc.
Experience working in Linux Environments with good command of shell, python, awk, sed
Motivation to understand/develop an understanding of various financial data elements and how they are used for trading
Ability to work collaboratively with a team and demonstrate passion for developing high-quality software.
Proven experience in hands-on development and deployment of significant components into production environments.
Strong analytical and debugging skills to support active production systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, enabling effective internal and external client communication.
Ability to manage multiple initiatives concurrently.
Proficiency in collaborating with distributed users and development teams across different time zones.

APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS:
CURRENT PENN STATE EMPLOYEE (faculty, staff, technical service, or student), please login to Workday to complete the internal application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.
CURRENT PENN STATE STUDENT (not employed previously at the university) and seeking employment with Penn State, please login to Workday to complete the student application process. Please do not apply here, apply internally through Workday.

POSITION SPECIFICS
Your working location will be fully on-site located in State College, PA. This role requires periodic travel to remote locations.
We are searching for a highly motivated Robotics Engineer to join the Autonomy and Emerging Technology (AET) Department at the Applied Research Laboratory (ARL) at Penn State. AET serves as ARL’s innovation hub for developing and evaluating advanced capabilities in the Subsea and Seabed Warfare (SSW) mission space. This role will work at the intersection of autonomy, underwater robotics, and prototype system integration to rapidly transition new technologies to Navy sponsors. Our team is expanding to support SSW mission area.
ARL is an authorized DoD SkillBridge partner and welcomes all transitioning military members to apply.
You will:
Technical: Develop/contribute to system and sub-system software implementation, test/evaluation and deployment of autonomy for UxVs, including adaptive mission behaviors, environmental awareness, distributed autonomy, multi-vehicle coordination, and integration of autonomy with UxV sensors and payloads. Drive advancements in UxV simulation, field testing, and fleet-relevant autonomy capabilities
Team Work: Work within a multidisciplinary team of software/systems engineers working across undersea navigation, endurance optimization, acoustic communications, environmental modeling, and autonomy-enabled CONOPS
Simulation and Test: Work within a team of engineers to develop and test prototype architecture solutions through testing with: software-in-the-loop (SIL); hardware-in-the-loop (HIL); and on-water testing
Collaboration: Interact and collaborate regularly with software team, project lead and other collaborators throughout the lab
Additional responsibilities for higher-level position includes:
Conduct independent and collaborative research, development, testing, and evaluation activities to solve complex scientific and engineering challenges supporting Department of Defense sponsors and national security missions
Investigate, evaluate, and apply established and emerging engineering principles, scientific methodologies, and advanced technologies to develop innovative technical solutions
Plan, perform, and lead analytical studies, modeling and simulation, laboratory experimentation, field testing, and prototype demonstrations to validate engineering concepts and system performance
Design, develop, integrate, analyze, and evaluate complex hardware, software, embedded systems, sensors, communications systems, electromechanical systems, or other mission-critical technologies within assigned technical disciplines
Apply systems engineering principles throughout the project lifecycle, including requirements development, architecture definition, design trade studies, integration, verification, validation, risk management, and configuration management
Develop experimental plans, test procedures, data collection methodologies, and performance metrics; analyze results to identify technical issues, validate assumptions, and recommend design improvements
Required Skills/Experience areas include:
C/C++, Python, Java, or similar
Agile software methodologies
DevSecOps - specifically with GitLab and/or Atlassian tools (JIRA, Bitbucket, Confluence)
Design of software using containerization technologies (Open Container Initiative, Docker, K8s/K3s) and micro-service architectures
Test and evaluation of software
Preferred Skills/Experience areas include:
UxV systems, including platforms, mission payloads, launch and recovery, acoustic comms, and energy management
Oceanography, seabed features, and environmental data used for UxV autonomy
Past success supporting Navy missions, operational training, or UxV fleet experimentation
Development or use of UxV simulation frameworks (e.g., platform, payload, or environmental modeling)
Autonomy for unmanned systems including autonomy architectures, behavior frameworks and mission planning for undersea missions, undersea navigation and perception autonomy behaviors, and autonomy standards for UxVs (e.g., MOSA, A-GRA, UMAA, PCX)
UXV simulation, evaluation, and verification environments
Test and evaluation of maritime platforms
Contribute to research in vehicle autonomy, machine learning, autonomous systems simulation/evaluation, undersea sensors, vehicle systems
Previous Navy systems development as related to unmanned systems
Technical experience related to the development of software for autonomous or unmanned systems is highly desired
Advanced degree in Engineer, Computer Science, Software, Machine Learning
Current eligibility for access to classified information at the Secret level or higher and may be subject to a government background investigation to upgrade clearance eligibility, if required

Design, develop, and maintain efficient, reusable, and reliable code
Implement complex software solutions that meet business requirements
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define, design, and ship new features
Identify and resolve performance bottlenecks and bugs

Comfort with Git, pull requests, code review and running tests in CI/CD pipelines.
Persistence when debugging: reading logs, inspecting network calls and querying databases.
Clear written communication: bug reports, test plans and short async status updates.

Testing data pipelines and orchestration tools (Airflow, dbt, Great Expectations, Elementary) or data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery).

Testing AI agents or MCP servers, or using AI coding assistants to speed up test writing and exploratory testing.

Performance and load testing (k6, Locust, JMeter).
Experience with ad tech, digital media or large third-party platform APIs (Google Ads, Meta, TikTok, Snap).
Frontend knowledge (React) to test framework upgrades and migrations.
Security basics for test environments, such as managing secrets for test accounts.

Collaborate with data operations to design task curricula and evaluation protocols that stress-test model capabilities across environment types
Own environment deployment and reliability: CI/CD pipelines, automated testing of environment configurations, and monitoring for drift or breakage across versions
Rapidly prototype new environment types as client and internal requirements evolve, moving from spec to working system in days, not weeks

Comfort working with browser automation frameworks or terminal interaction tooling
Strong debugging instincts—you can trace failures across process boundaries, container layers, and network calls
Ability to read and implement from academic papers and open-source benchmark repositories without extensive hand-holding
Preferred
Direct experience building or contributing to RL environments (Gymnasium/Gym, PettingZoo, or custom environment implementations)
Experience with agentic AI evaluation frameworks (SWE-bench, WebArena, OSWorld, TerminalBench, or similar)
Familiarity with GCP or AWS infrastructure (Compute Engine, ECS/EKS, Cloud Build)
Prior work at an AI data company, ML platform company, or AI research lab
Contributions to open-source projects in the RL, agents, or dev-tools space
Candidate Archetype
The ideal candidate is a strong software engineer first, with genuine curiosity and working knowledge of reinforcement learning. You’ve probably built infrastructure or developer tooling at a startup or mid-stage company, and you’ve been pulled toward the ML/AI space—maybe through side projects, open-source contributions, or a prior role adjacent to an ML team. You’re the kind of engineer who reads an RL benchmark paper and immediately thinks about how to make the environment more robust, not how to improve the policy gradient.

ClarityPay is seeking Forward Deployed Engineers to embed with the teams that run the company and turn how they work into dependable, AI-native systems. You will sit with process owners in finance, credit and portfolio risk, servicing and collections, and operations; scope the problem with them before building; ship agents, controls and automations into production; and stay through adoption as the named secondary owner of the process. You will join the Data & AI organization, working alongside engineers in New York and India on a shared platform, and alongside Product and Engineering you will build external-facing AI solutions for merchants and partners on the ClarityPay platform. You will use AI tooling to make the build the easy part, and you will be measured on what is adopted and relied upon, not on what is demoed.

Embed with process owners to map how the work actually runs, scope the problem with them before building, and agree success criteria and a baseline up front.
Own delivery end to end — discovery, technical scoping, system design, build and production rollout — and stay through adoption as the named secondary owner of the process.
Choose the simplest dependable solution: simplify or remove a step before automating it, then pick a scheduled job, a triggered job, or a bounded agent with a defined mandate, action set, escalation owner and pause conditions.
Write evaluations for everything you ship: prove the output is correct before a team depends on it, and re-check it as models, data and processes change.
Instrument what you build, and the processes around it, with detective (“day-zero”) controls — thresholds, exception inventories and alerting, each with an action path and a named owner — so a breach surfaces the same day, not at month-end.

Work inside ClarityPay’s controls for AI — evaluate before exposure, bound the exposure, keep a person at the gate — and propose where a human must review, where automation may act unattended, and what gets logged.

Continually promote and apply ClarityPay values; be a role model of trust and integrity.

Desktop and spreadsheet-based reporting processes are inventoried, baselined and moved onto AI agentic systems running on governed data, with a person at the gate where judgment is needed.
Recurring performance reporting — portfolio, collections, servicing and finance — is produced by agents from governed metrics rather than manual pulls, on time and traceable to source.
Day-zero controls are live in your first processes, each with a threshold, an action path and a named owner, so breaches surface the same day.
The effort returned is measured against the baseline, net of review, exceptions and maintenance, and reported to executives.
At least one external-facing solution for merchants or partners is in production and adopted.
The patterns, evals and agent-harness standards you built are reused by the next deployment.

About Us
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Destro AI is building the intelligence layer for robotics — the system that coordinates robots, humans, and workflows across complex real-world operations. Schedule Expectations
This is a field deployment role, not a standard office-hours position. Warehouse operations run multiple shifts, and go-lives, incidents, and integrations are not confined to business hours.
Regular work outside standard business hours should be expected, including nights and weekends. Go-lives are frequently scheduled during off-hours or weekend downtime windows to avoid disrupting customer operations.

Software

Design and build internal tools that make field deployments faster and more repeatable.
Translate field learnings into production-hardening fixes and improvements in the core codebase.
Maintain clear technical documentation and runbooks so issues can be diagnosed consistently across sites.
Field Deployment
Deploy and validate Destro's software stack in live warehouses, working directly with customer operations, IT, and engineering teams.
Own production issues end-to-end during launch and stabilization, including off-hours incidents.
Improve uptime, throughput, and reliability of deployed systems through both code and infrastructure changes.
Systems and Infrastructure
Build and maintain containerized services (Docker Compose) running on Destro-managed servers and edge devices.
Work with cloud infrastructure (GCP) for image management, versioning, and deployment tooling.
Configure and troubleshoot networking, including VLANs, DHCP, internal DNS, and certificate-based service security.
Debug across the full stack: robot state faults, sensor issues, API failures, container networking, database queries, and monitoring dashboards.

2 to 6 years of experience in systems engineering, robotics software, backend engineering, infrastructure, or field engineering, with genuine software development experience rather than field support alone.
Comfortable being paged off-hours and traveling on short notice.
Able to operate independently in ambiguous, high-pressure environments without a fully specified solution.
Calm under pressure, direct with customers, and demonstrates strong ownership.
Technical Skills
Required
Strong Python or C++, with the ability to write maintainable, production-grade code.
Hands-on Docker/Docker Compose experience, including building, deploying, debugging, and versioning images.
Linux/server administration: command line, logs, processes, systemd, firewalls.

Proficiency with Git and standard software development workflows.

Company Description
Etsy is the global marketplace for unique and creative goods. We build, power, and evolve the tools and technologies that connect millions of entrepreneurs with millions of buyers around the world. As an Etsy employee, you will tackle unique, meaningful, and large-scale problems alongside passionate coworkers, all the while making a rewarding impact and Keeping Commerce Human.
We believe exceptional companies are built by exceptional teams, and we're intentional about it. That means hiring great people, setting them up for success from day one, and giving them real reasons to grow their careers here. We invest in development that goes beyond promotions, and we foster the trust and relationships that help people do their best work together.
What’s the role?
Etsy is hiring a Machine Learning Engineer II to join the Fulfillment ML team. Our team owns the machine learning that powers Etsy's shipping and delivery experience - models that help buyers see accurate delivery estimates, help sellers price and ship their orders accurately, and help Etsy make smart fulfillment decisions at scale. Examples of models we own include Estimated Delivery Date (EDD) prediction, shipping price prediction, transit-time modeling, and delivery-risk signals. We're a multi-functional group of engineers, applied scientists, and product managers, and we partner closely with data scientists, designers, and product-facing engineering teams across Etsy.
This role combines ML platform engineering with hands-on applied ML work. On the platform side, you'll build and operate the pipelines, orchestration, and tooling that take our models from training through validation, promotion, and inference in production. On the applied side, you'll partner with senior teammates on model evaluation, backtests, tuning, and readiness reviews - you're not expected to design new model architectures yourself, but you will work deeply with the models, learn how they behave, and grow your applied ML expertise over time.
This is a great opportunity for a strong software engineer early in their ML career who wants to level up on both the systems side and the modeling side, inside a mature MLOps stack that ships model predictions to millions of Etsy buyers and sellers every day.
This is a full-time position reporting to the Engineering Manager, Fulfillment ML.
What's this team like at Etsy?
Fulfillment ML owns the machine learning behind Etsy's shipping and delivery experience - across buyer-facing surfaces like Search, Listing, Cart, and Checkout, and across seller-facing tools. Our team includes MLEs, applied scientists, and platform engineers. New model design is usually led by senior teammates; the surrounding applied ML work (evaluation, backtests, tuning, readiness) and the platform/infrastructure work are shared responsibilities across the team, including this role. Our stack includes Python, PyTorch, Ray, Spark, Airflow, Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI), Dataproc, BigQuery, and GCS.
Here's a Taste Of The Problems We're Solving
How do we predict when an order will arrive at a buyer's door across dozens of countries, carriers, and shipping methods?
How do we tell buyers what's likely to arrive by a given date without underpromising or overpromising?
How do we spot delivery risk early enough to help sellers and buyers make good decisions?
