Back
Careers at Pitch Aeronautics Inc.
Flight Controls Engineer
Pitch Aeronautics Inc. Flight Controls Engineer Boise, ID
Full time
Apply for Flight Controls Engineer
Astria is a custom heavy-lift drone that combines lift motors with a cyclorotor for lateral force. It runs our own Simulink-built controllers on PX4-based flight hardware. It flies real installs on utility lines today. You'll contribute to controller changes from idea to flight. That means modeling the vehicle, designing and tuning the controller, testing it on the stand, flying it with our pilots, and reading the logs to find out what actually happened. It's a small team, so you'll be in the shop and in the field, not just at a desk. We're an AI-driven company. AI tooling runs throughout our engineering workflow, including MATLAB and Simulink work, log analysis, and simulation.
About Pitch Aeronautics Inc.
Pitch Aeronautics (www.pitchaero.com) is a rapidly growing startup creating game-changing solutions for the utility industry. Pitch has developed a drone to install our line sensor, bird diverters, and other equipment on power lines. Our drone-deployable line sensors wirelessly transmit environmental and line characteristics to an online secure API to help utilities push more power through existing lines, prevent wildfires, and improve grid reliability.
At Pitch we’ve fostered a collaborative, fun, “get-stuff-done” working environment. We believe in moving fast and creating products and prototypes rapidly. If you’re looking for a place where you can make a difference on day one, be empowered to achieve, and love working in small teams, we want to meet you!
Description
Responsibilities
Design, model, and tune flight controllers (attitude, position, altitude, yaw, trim) in MATLAB/Simulink and deploy them to PX4-based flight hardware.
Build and maintain vehicle dynamics models, including the cyclorotor, and extend our simulation capability (e.g., Gazebo, SITL).
Write test plans and run test-stand and flight tests with the drone ops crew.
Analyze flight logs (PX4 ULog) for tracking error, motor saturation, and vibration, and build tools that make that analysis faster.
Make the controller robust to estimator events such as EKF resets, IMU switches, and GPS dropouts.
Characterize propulsion (thrust vs. RPM, motor and prop selection) and fold the results back into the control code.
Develop control for aerial manipulation: precise lateral positioning, wind rejection, and contact with the conductor during sensor install and removal.
Configure and integrate motor controllers over DroneCAN.
Document controller design decisions and changes, manage control code in Git, and post clear updates for the team.
Mentor technicians and interns, and work with pilots on how the aircraft feels to fly.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering, or a related field, with a focus on controls.
3+ years designing and testing control systems for UAVs, aircraft, or robots, or a graduate degree with significant hands-on flight-test work.
Strong MATLAB/Simulink skills, including code generation for embedded targets.
Solid grounding in classical control: PID/PD design, feedforward, saturation and anti-windup, rate and jerk limiting, and frequency-domain analysis.
Hands-on flight or hardware testing experience, including reading logs to diagnose problems.
Python for data analysis and tooling; Git.
Clear technical writing.
Able to work on-site in Boise and travel occasionally for field tests and installs.
Desired Qualifications
Experience with PX4 or ArduPilot internals (uORB, EKF2) and Pixhawk/Cube hardware.
Multirotor or unconventional rotorcraft dynamics; cyclorotor experience is a big plus.
Aerial manipulation or contact control.
State estimation and sensor fusion.
Simulation with Gazebo, SITL, or HITL.
CAN/DroneCAN and motor controller integration.
FAA Part 107 certificate or piloting experience.
Master's or PhD in controls, robotics, or aerospace.
Fluency with AI assistants in engineering work, and enough depth to catch them when they're wrong.

About The Role
What we do
Delphi, Uber's Lever Efficiency team, builds the system Uber uses to recommend how to invest billions of dollars per year across its marketplace supply and demand levers: courier pricing (supply), courier incentives (supply), delivery and service fees (demand), user promotions (demand), etc. Starting with Uber's Delivery Marketplace business, we turn experiment results into a measure of each lever's incremental value in a common currency and publish it in a dashboard that refreshes automatically. We're also building a budget allocation tool that recommends how to move budget between levers. We work day to day with data scientists, product, operations, and finance.
Why it matters
Today each lever spends against its own budget target, even after it starts hitting diminishing returns. A trusted, comparable measure of what each lever returns lets Uber move money to where it does the most good: more reliable deliveries for customers, more earning opportunities for couriers, and more long-term growth for every dollar spent. The hard part is making the numbers trustworthy enough that Operations and Finance leaders act on them. Then the recommendations have to be proven with well-designed experiments. That's the system you'll help build.

Jupyter Notebooks
Fullstack development experience (BE, FE, Data Pipelines), this project involves a full suite of development surfaces across UI, backend, and data.
Experience developing internal tooling used by Ops, Engineers, Finance, Scientists, etc.
What the Candidate Will Do
Build and own data pipelines (Spark, Hive, scheduled workflows) that recompute lever-efficiency estimates from experiment and marketplace data every week. Include data-quality checks, freshness alerts and backfills.
Build backend services and APIs in Go that store and serve efficiency estimates and budget recommendations.
Ship full-stack features in the web app: interactive dashboards and a budget allocation tool used by Operations, Finance, Product, and Science.
Work with data scientists to turn notebook prototypes into production code. This includes confidence intervals, corrections for network effects, forecasts, and an optimizer that moves budget between levers within real constraints, such as fixed total spend and capped weekly changes.
Work with Uber's experimentation platform to run experiments that test budget moves (switchbacks, geo experiments, synthetic control), and automate reading their results into the dashboard.

Document methodology and system design so partners can trust and reuse the numbers.

The OCI Robotics Cloud team is developing a platform that enables customers to securely connect robots to the cloud and manage them through consistent services for identity, missions, fleet operations, telemetry, digital twins, and software lifecycle management.
We’re also building an
AI-assisted robot onboarding platform
designed to make integrating a new robot dramatically easier. Instead of writing every integration from scratch, engineers will use standardized specifications, APIs, SDKs, and reusable edge adapters to connect robots from different vendors to OCI.
As a
Senior Platform Software Engineer
, you’ll build the cloud and edge software that makes this possible. You’ll own meaningful features end-to-end, work on real distributed-systems problems, and gain hands-on experience at the intersection of cloud infrastructure, robotics, and AI.
Responsibilities
What You’ll Do
Design and implement production cloud services for robot registration, identity, fleet operations, mission execution, telemetry, digital twins, and software lifecycle management.
Build scalable REST APIs and backend services using modern cloud-native architectures.
Develop SDKs, service contracts, and edge components used to connect robots to OCI.
Implement reusable robot adapters and integration frameworks for different robot vendors and protocols.
Build components of AI-assisted onboarding workflows that generate specifications, integration code, and developer guidance.
Integrate cloud services with robots, simulators, autonomous systems, and edge environments.
Improve service reliability, observability, performance, security, and operational tooling.
Debug issues across cloud services, networks, edge software, and robot integrations.
Write high-quality, maintainable, tested production code and participate actively in code and design reviews.
Collaborate with experienced engineers across robotics, AI, security, and OCI infrastructure teams.

BS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
3+ years of professional software development experience.
Strong programming skills in one or more languages such as Go, Java, Python, or C++.
Experience building backend services, APIs, or distributed applications.
Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, or similar cloud-native technologies.
Solid understanding of software design, testing, debugging, and production engineering.
Ability to independently own and deliver well-scoped technical projects.
Strong communication and collaboration skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with ROS 2 or robotics software development.
Familiarity with DDS, MQTT, OPC-UA, VDA5050, or related protocols.
Experience integrating devices, robots, autonomous systems, or edge software with cloud services.
Familiarity with Kubernetes-based platforms and cloud-to-edge architectures.
Understanding of robot navigation, localization, perception, mission execution, or fleet management.
Experience with NVIDIA Isaac Sim, Gazebo, Webots, or similar simulation tools.
Exposure to LLMs, AI agents, vision-language models, code generation, or AI-assisted developer tools.
Interest in developer platforms, SDKs, APIs, and extensible integration frameworks.
Why This Role Is Different
This role combines
cloud engineering with real-world robotics
.

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44807.description_preview:
The role
At Mach9, Digital Surveyor turns massive LiDAR datasets into precise CAD deliverables, automating work that currently takes surveyors and engineers weeks. Making that possible in a browser requires a 3D engine that can render tens of millions of points while supporting CAD-grade picking, clipping, snapping, and measurement. You'll work directly on that engine and the tools built on it.
This role is ideal for an early-career engineer with a strong foundation in 3D math who wants to work on a real production renderer, not a demo.
You'll do well here if you enjoy digging into difficult technical problems and building software that stays fast and reliable on large, messy real-world datasets. When the right approach isn't obvious, you'll research how others have solved similar problems, test your assumptions, and choose a practical solution. Our engineers are trusted to own their work and drive meaningful outcomes.
Where you will make an impact
Build 3D tools that surveyors use to inspect point clouds and create precise engineering drawings
Extend our point-cloud renderer and GPU picking system
Solve geometry problems behind clipping, snapping, construction planes, and camera controls
Find and fix performance problems that appear with large real-world datasets
Improve the shared rendering and interaction systems behind our CAD tools
What you bring
A strong foundation in 3D math and spatial reasoning, including transforms, planes, and projections
Experience building software through coursework, personal projects, internships, or full-time work
The ability to read and change code you did not write
Attention to correctness and performance
Sound judgment about when to refine a solution and when to ship it
Experience with TypeScript and browser graphics, or comparable experience writing performance-sensitive graphics code in a statically typed language
The initiative to investigate problems, ask useful questions, and finish what you start
Bonus experience
WebGL, GLSL, Three.js, Cesium, or another real-time graphics system
Point clouds, geospatial data, or large-coordinate rendering
Experience applying geometry, spatial algorithms, or numerical methods to open-ended problems with noisy data and real-world tradeoffs
CAD, mapping, visualization, robotics, or game-engine projects
About Mach9
Mach9 is transforming civil infrastructure design with AI-powered geospatial tools. Our platform accelerates the creation of engineering deliverables from raw data, cutting manual drafting time by 96×. Trusted by global leaders in engineering and construction, we're backed by Y Combinator, Quiet Capital, and top founders and executives from Cruise, Autodesk, Adobe, and DoorDash.
We believe the needs of a startup benefit from an in-person culture. The team works out of our office in SoMa, with the flexibility to work from home when needed.

Experience working with large language models, generative AI, or agentic systems—either in research, production, or applied engineering

Familiarity with government or public sector technology environments (federal civilian agencies, state/local gov, or regulated industries like healthcare, finance, or infrastructure)
Strong product sensibility: ability to translate ambiguous stakeholder needs into concrete technical solutions
Demonstrated ability to write clean, maintainable, high-performance code under tight timelines
Exceptional problem-solving skills and intellectual curiosity—you thrive on hard, ambiguous challenges.
Excellent communication skills; you can explain complex technical concepts to non-technical partners clearly and concisely.

DataVisor is the world’s leading AI-powered Fraud and Risk Platform that delivers the best overall detection coverage in the industry.With an open SaaS platform that supports easy consolidation and enrichment of any data, DataVisor's fraud and anti-money laundering (AML) solutions scale infinitely and enable organizations to act on fast-evolving fraud and money laundering activities in real time.Its patented unsupervised machine learning technology, advanced device intelligence, powerful decision engine, and investigation tools work together to provide significant performance lift from day one.DataVisor's platform is architected to support multiple use cases across different business units flexibly, dramatically lowering total cost of ownership compared to legacy point solutions.DataVisor is recognized as an industry leader and has been adopted by many Fortune 500 companies across the globe.
Our award-winning software platform is powered by a team of world-class experts in big data, machine learning, security, and scalable infrastructure. Our culture is open, positive, collaborative, and results-driven.Come join us!
Role Summary
We are hiring a Software Engineer to build the automation that lets a small team deliver fraud and AML solutions to many clients at once.
You will build internal tooling the Solutions team uses every day — Claude Code plugins, skills and MCP servers in our internal plugin marketplace — and integrate them with our AI Sandbox, the Vera platform, and the APIs behind them. You will also work directly on client onboarding: standing up tenants from solution templates, parsing third-party data and responses, wiring up integrations, and validating end to end that the right alerts actually fire.
This is a production software engineering role. What we are really hiring for is the instinct to turn something one client needed into something every client gets. Machine learning experience is not required, and neither is a fraud or AML background — both are learnable, and we would rather have an engineer who ships.
This role is open at both junior and senior levels.
Primary responsibilities
Build Automation Tooling: Design and ship the plugins, skills and MCP servers the Solutions team runs — tenant creation, configuration copying, onboarding flows, on-call helpers — in Python and shell.
Make It Reusable: Turn one-off solutions into tooling that works for every client. This is the core of the job, not an afterthought.
Integrate with the Platform: Connect tooling to the AI Sandbox, Vera and internal platform APIs, and keep it working across sandbox, preprod and production tenants.
Support Client Onboarding: Work hands-on on live onboardings — tenant setup from templates, schema and response parsing, third-party integrations over SFTP and API, and end-to-end validation that the right alerts fire.
Serve Your Users: What you build is used by core engineering, product, delivery, customer support and technical account management. Understanding what each of them needs, and keeping them informed, is part of the work.
Own Your Projects: Scope, sequence and deliver your own work, and say clearly where it stands.
Requirements
Qualifications
Experience: At least 1 year of full-time professional software engineering experience building and shipping production systems. Internships are not counted toward this minimum. We are open on level — we care more about what you have built than how long you have been building.
Education: BS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or Software Engineering. MS preferred. We also consider other STEM degrees alongside a record of shipped production software.
Shipped Software: Demonstrated experience delivering working software end to end — not prototypes or notebooks.
Coding Proficiency: Strong, production-grade Python — the primary language for this team's automation and tooling. Java is expected for senior candidates and preferred for junior ones: our core platform is built in Java, and you will work across both over time. Comfort with shell, and with reading unfamiliar codebases, matters as much as either language.
Cloud and Containers: Experience with AWS and containerization (Docker/Kubernetes).
Built for Others: Evidence of building something other people then used — an internal tool, a library, a plugin, a template, a service another team depends on.
Collaboration and Ownership: Able to work across team boundaries, take end-to-end ownership, and operate where the path is not already defined.
Preferred qualifications
Java, if you are applying at a junior level — our core platform is built in it.
TypeScript — solution features often land in our front end.
LLM-powered agent workflows — LangChain/LangGraph, multi-agent orchestration, tool calling or RAG — for production or internal platforms.
Distributed data frameworks such as Spark, Kafka or Flink.
Experience deploying or maintaining machine learning models in production.
Analytical databases and large-scale data exploration (ClickHouse or other columnar stores).
Real-time decision engines or stateful stream processing.
Domain knowledge in fraud or risk — a plus, never a requirement.
Benefits
Base Salary: 130K – 250K
Total Compensation: Includes Base + Performance Bonus + Equity Options.
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.
Discretionary Time Off Policy (DTO) and paid holidays.
Opportunities for R&D exploration and professional development.
Regular team-building events and a collaborative, innovative culture.

all dedicated to redefining the relationship between people and their vehicles for millions of customers.
As a Ford Motor Company subsidiary, we operate independently to develop automated driving technology at the speed of a technology startup. Latitude is headquartered in Pittsburgh with engineering centers in Dearborn, Mich., and Palo Alto, Calif.
Meet The Team
The Virtual Test Ecosystem (VTE) team ensures that our simulation (fully synthetic) and resimulation (replay engine using vehicle logs) workflows run efficiently and reliably at large scale. We use a mix of open source and cloud provider services to implement a processing framework that’s cloud-agnostic as well as capable of running on-prem. The results of these simulations is business-critical for us - they’re used in order to allow autonomy developers and testers to do large-scale safety and performance testing of changes prior to in-vehicle testing. We interact with engineers throughout the onboard and offboard stack in order to ensure smooth end-to-end capabilities.
What You’ll Do
We run vehicle simulations at unprecedented scales in order to ensure we’re releasing a safe product. You’ll support this via improvements to our sim/resim cloud framework and applications that run on this framework. In terms of implementation, this involves a lot of Python coding, interacting with open source packages and various AWS/GCP services. In terms of analysis, we’re constantly looking for bottlenecks that limit scalability or otherwise hinder performance. You’ll put together benchmarking to identify these spots and associated dashboards to track and summarize the information. Then armed with that information, you’ll implement solutions to increase efficiency.
It’s not enough to have a framework that is functional - it needs to be intuitive and easy to use. We take our best guesses at this, but things evolve over time based on user interaction - both direct feedback as well as realizing how users are accidentally misusing or misinterpreting the results. VTE supports autonomy, systems, test, and a variety of other teams across the organization. Having an eye for how the system is being used, what users need, and a willingness to engage with these users on future improvements is critical.
We also can’t build it all, so we want to make the framework well-documented and as self-serve as possible for others to extend it (while being there to answer questions). For example, when there’s a new portion of the autonomy stack, we want that autonomy team to be able to update resim to add it in themselves so that they can iterate quickly.
In order to run logs through resim, we need to first know what logs are interesting. You’ll contribute to the ecosystem of how we manage storing and searching for these logs efficiently, including how we automate indexing the interesting actors and interactions in a scene and how we determine our dataset coverage.
Once we’ve run resim, we want to do something with the updated logs. Frequently this involves metrics to analyze the AV’s performance; these metrics could range from low-level performance of a particular detector in the stack to if the AV is meeting high-level business objectives. You’ll both work on the sim/resim cloud framework implementation to make this easy for all developers to add in their metrics and support the metrics implementation themselves as needs arise.

Summary
About the Product
Concierge is Guidewire's omnichannel AI agent for P&C carriers. It answers the phone when a policyholder has just had an accident, takes first notice of loss, asks the questions a good adjuster would ask, and writes a clean claim into ClaimCenter. It runs in production today with real carriers and real policyholders, not as a demo.
Two things make this harder than a typical chatbot. First, it has synchronous voice: latency is a product requirement, not a metric on a dashboard. Second, FNOL is a regulated event where the quality of the intake determines the eventual cost of the claim. A missed question early is a bigger loss reserve later.
The Role
You will build, evaluate, and harden the agent itself: the orchestration, the context it sees, the tools it can call, and the evals that tell us whether a change made it better or just different.
Our rollout philosophy is a dimmer, not a light switch. We widen the agent's autonomy one notch at a time, and every notch has to be earned with evidence. Much of your work is producing that evidence, then acting on what it says.
Job Description
What you'll do
Own end-to-end slices of the agent: prompt and context architecture, retrieval over policy and coverage data, tool and API calls into core claims systems, and handoff to a human when the agent should stop.
Build and run the eval loop, golden sets, trajectory evaluation, LLM-as-judge, error analysis on real production call traces, and make it the thing that gates releases.
Drive containment and resolution rates up without trading away accuracy, and instrument the system well enough that we can tell which of the two moved.
Work directly on the voice path: turn-taking, interruption, latency budgets, and the telephony layer underneath (LiveKit, SIP).
Sit in on carrier calls and listen to recordings. The best fixes usually come from hearing where the conversation went sideways, not from reading the logs.
What We're Looking For
Building and deploying AI applications. You've shipped an LLM application that real users depend on, and you know that the hard part is that the output is not predictable. You're fluent in the building blocks LLMs, context engineering, RAG, agentic workflows, and you have real ML and deep learning depth underneath that fluency. Most importantly, you know how to make an unpredictable system behave predictably enough to trust: disciplined evals, error analysis, and statistical measurement rather than vibes and a handful of spot checks.
Software engineering fundamentals. You can reason about cost, latency, reliability, and scalability as tradeoffs rather than goals, and you know which ones you're making. You've designed data stores and distributed systems, you write tests, and you take security and privacy seriously while advocating CI/CD process automation. We handle claims data, recorded calls, and PII under carrier and regulatory scrutiny.
Using coding agents. You work with coding agents daily and you're good at it: managing their context, deciding when a spec is worth writing and when it isn't, giving them verifiers so they can close their own loops, and knowing when to intervene versus leave them alone. You also keep changing how you work as the tooling changes, rather than settling into a 2025 workflow.
Shaping the build. You won't be handed a finished spec. You'll be in the room where we decide what the agent should do next, which means you need product sense and enough insurance context to argue about it. You'll know when to put an MVP in front of a carrier next week and when a claims workflow demands that we slow down and get it right the first time.
Underneath all four: you keep learning. This field looks different every six months and we expect to keep changing our minds.
Nice to have
Real-time or streaming voice systems (ASR, TTS, telephony, SBC/SIPREC)
Insurance, claims, or another regulated domain where being wrong has a cost attached
Experience building internal eval or observability tooling other engineers actually adopted.
Experience in Machine learning principles, or have experience in model experimentations, training and deploying models in Productions.
Experience in P&C Insurance or exposure to Guidewire products and services.
Prompt or pipeline optimization frameworks (DSPy, GEPA) applied to a production system
How To Apply
Send a short note about something you shipped where the model's unpredictability was the central problem, and what you did about it. We care more about that than about a list of frameworks.

About Us
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
The Job
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
About You
You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.
You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.
You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.
Nice to have:
Developer-facing products, protocol or gateway work, or infrastructure at scale.
Background in security, identity, or permission systems.
Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.
Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.
What we offer:
Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.
Unusual scope and ownership of features that ship to enterprise customers.
Building and deploying agents on the same platform we sell.
Direct access to the founders, customer context, and product direction, with mentorship as you grow.
Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
About The Team
As a Software Manufacturing Test Engineer, you will build, scale, and maintain the software that drives our manufacturing test systems. In this role, your primary focus will be developing production software that directly tests complex hardware systems, integrates with laboratory instrumentation and DAQs, and manages the data these stations produce. You will bridge low-level hardware control with high-level test automation by writing robust, reliable production code in Python and C# targeting Linux/Unix (and ideally NixOS) runtime environments.
To ensure our hardware meets mission-critical quality and production throughput demands, every Software Manufacturing Test Engineer is expected to derive software test requirements from hardware schematics and system specifications, author automated test sequences, and deploy complete software suites to factory test racks. You will work closely with development and firmware engineers to refine test coverage as product designs evolve, resolve complex hardware-software integration failures on the floor, and ensure deterministic software deployments across our manufacturing line.
What You'll Do
Maintain ownership of software manufacturing test activities in production, ensuring test station uptime, operator usability, and smooth factory throughput
Develop and maintain PLC-integrated station control software — commanding industrial controllers over Modbus TCP for rig actuation, interlocks, and sensor acquisition — and maintain the tag/address index as PLC programs evolve, including tooling that imports controller tag exports and validates them against the station's expected schema
Build hardware-free simulation environments (containerized station images, virtual CAN replay, device simulators) so test software is developed and regression-tested without occupying hardware
Design, build, and maintain production software manufacturing test suites primarily in Python (for hardware control, test sequencing, and instrument automation) and C# (for test executives, operator interfaces, and background services)
Integrate software manufacturing test applications directly with sensors, DAQs, programmable power supplies, electronic loads, and vehicle compute hardware
Implement low-level hardware communication using embedded protocols including UART, CAN, and RS-485 / RS-232 to command, flash, and validate devices under test (DUTs)
Deploy, configure, and debug software manufacturing test systems running on Linux/Unix platforms using terminal command-line tools, SSH, and network debugging utilities
Leverage Nix and NixOS to manage reproducible software manufacturing test environments, eliminating dependency drift between engineering development benches and production line stations
Collaborate with hardware and firmware engineers during early-stage product development (NPI) to define software manufacturing test requirements, coverage, APIs, and pass/fail limits
Automate software manufacturing test execution across various levels of assembly, from PCBA-level functional test (FCT) up to full-system and Environmental Stress Screening (ESS) checkouts
Provide hands-on troubleshooting and root-cause analysis (RCCA) for complex electrical, firmware, and software manufacturing test issues found on the line
Log parametric test data and integrate software manufacturing test stations with database systems (using SQL queries as needed) and Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) to maintain complete hardware traceability
Develop clear operator interfaces, error-handling mechanisms, and software manufacturing test troubleshooting logs to assist technicians during hardware failures
Support continuous improvement initiatives to optimize software manufacturing test sequences, shorten cycle times, and increase test coverage without sacrificing quality
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related fields
3+ years of relevant industry experience as a Software Manufacturing Test Engineer, or in an equivalent role with an emphasis on software development for hardware test automation, lab automation, or manufacturing environments
Strong proficiency writing production code in Python for software manufacturing test automation, device control, and data handling

This role helps the scientists who build and operate QuEra's neutral-atom quantum computers program those machines effectively. Turn user problems into minimal reproducible reports, regression tests and focused fixes, and work with the compiler team on larger language or IR changes.

Experience debugging unfamiliar code and reducing complex failures to minimal reproductions.
Familiarity with the full software lifecycle: version control, code review, testing, CI/CD, logging, profiling, debugging and documentation.

About Elveo
Elveo is what happens when two pioneers in direct-to-device (D2D) communications join forces. Elveo brings together a combined 20 years of expertise to close the coverage gap for more than 50 mobile network operators (MNOs) and major distribution partners operating in 60+ countries worldwide.
That heritage and our technology powers what we call ‘elevated intelligence’ — a new approach that processes and adapts on orbit, delivering voice and data services straight to mobile users, IoT devices and machines across enterprise, government and humanitarian sectors worldwide.
As a team, we’re on a mission to deliver powerful compute and connectivity directly to individuals and objects everywhere on Earth.
Join us, and become part of a globally inclusive company that is transforming satellite communications from a niche service to an essential global infrastructure, and democratizing connectivity for billions worldwide.
Ready to take the next step? Join us.
About The Role
The Firmware Engineer at Elveo will develop the bare-metal and RTOS firmware that runs on the microcontrollers throughout our satellites — in the D2D communications payload and across the spacecraft bus. This role sits squarely between our Flight Software and Electrical Engineering teams: you will bring up new boards alongside the engineers who designed them, write the drivers and control loops that make that hardware useful, and define the interfaces that our Linux-based flight software uses to command and monitor it. The firmware will be developed and tested on lab hardware and on our "flatsat," a satellite prototype that simulates orbit operations, before it flies.
We build spacecraft fast! So, the ideal candidate enjoys taking a board from first power-on to flight-ready firmware on rapid timelines, and is equally comfortable reading a schematic, probing a bus with a logic analyzer, and reviewing a pull request. Firmware on orbit can only be fixed over a radio link, so we value engineers who design for robustness and recoverability from the start. This is a small team, so you will work alongside experienced engineers and take ownership of systems early.
Experience with satellites is not a requirement for this position. If you've shipped firmware for robotics, automotive, drones, medical devices, industrial controls, or similar, you'll find much of your experience translates directly. Title, scope, and compensation scale with experience.
Core Responsibilities
You Will Design, Develop, And Test Embedded Firmware For Microcontroller-based Subsystems Across The Spacecraft, Including Payload Control, Power, And Attitude Sensing And Actuation Electronics. This Includes
Developing bare-metal and RTOS firmware for microcontrollers, including device drivers, peripheral configuration, interrupt handling, and hardware abstraction layers.
Partnering with Electrical Engineering through schematic and design reviews, board bring-up, and debug of new hardware revisions.
Implementing communication with satellite devices and electronics using CAN, I2C, SPI, UART, RS-422, RS-485, and other protocols.
Defining and implementing the command, telemetry, and data interfaces between microcontroller firmware and Elveo's flight software.
Building bootloaders and firmware update mechanisms that can be safely exercised over a low-bandwidth radio link, with fallback images and recovery paths.
Designing for fault tolerance on orbit: watchdogs, brown-out and reset handling, memory protection and error detection, and graceful degradation.
Debugging hardware/firmware integration issues using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, JTAG/SWD debuggers, and other lab equipment.
Developing unit, hardware-in-the-loop, and flatsat tests for firmware, and integrating them into our CI pipelines.
Participating in design and code reviews, and documenting firmware designs, interfaces, and test procedures.
Supporting spacecraft integration, environmental testing, and on-orbit operations as needed.
Basic Qualifications
Proficiency in C for embedded systems, demonstrated through professional work, significant academic/personal projects, or open-source contributions.
Experience developing firmware for microcontrollers (e.g., ARM Cortex-M), including drivers for on-chip peripherals and external devices over SPI, I2C, UART, ethernet, CAN , etc.
Hands-on board bring-up and debug: reading schematics and datasheets, and using oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and JTAG/SWD debuggers.
Experience designing interrupt-driven, real-time firmware, either bare-metal or on an RTOS.
Experience writing automated tests for firmware you build and working with Git and CI/CD.
A bachelor's degree or higher in Computer, Electrical, Software, Aerospace, or related engineering field, or equivalent practical experience.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience writing bootloaders and in-field or over-the-air firmware update systems.
Experience working in small teams with a high degree of project ownership
Familiarity with radiation effects on electronics and their mitigations (e.g., EDAC/ECC, memory scrubbing, latch-up protection, redundancy).
Familiarity with embedded Linux and how microcontroller firmware interfaces with a Linux host.
Experience with FPGAs or mixed-signal electronics, including ADC/DAC interfacing.
Experience developing and testing hardware for SmallSats / CubeSats.
Experience with hardware-in-the-loop integration and testing.
Scripting experience in Python for test automation and lab tooling.

Amazon Leo is a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband network connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world.
We are looking for a software development engineer to join the founding cohort of the Engineering and R\&D team within Leo Space Security. The team defends the manufacturing lines, launch sites, and global ground infrastructure behind the constellation from the most sophisticated threat actors on the planet. You will build a neurosymbolic reasoning platform: large language model agents combined with a knowledge graph and real-time asset state store that ground every conclusion in verifiable fact, so every automated decision is auditable. The platform automates incident response, threat analysis, offensive security testing, and detection authoring, backed by a high-throughput streaming pipeline that takes a detection from concept to production in hours. The team is new and the surface area is wide: the features you ship become the system Leo's security teams run on from day one.
Export Control Requirement
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen.
Key job responsibilities
You will own building software features across the platform and deliver them end to end: clarify the requirements, write the design, ship the code, instrument the system, and keep it healthy in production. The features you own are concrete and high-consequence: the live state-of-the-world record that answers where every tracked device is, who last held it, and whether it is where it should be; consolidated detection that surfaces events from every Leo site type as one signal instead of siloed alarms; automated triage so security events arrive enriched and pre-adjudicated, with containment executed in seconds under human approval; self-service workflows that cut multi-day manual processes down to seconds; and the instrumentation that produces the metrics the security organization reports against. You will code independently, make design tradeoffs with guidance from the senior engineers who own the platform architecture, review your teammates' code, and operate what you build.
A day in the life
One morning you might ship a correlation feature that joins device, custody, and access events so triage surfaces a pattern no single data source shows. That afternoon you could be debugging why a detection's latency regressed, profiling the pipeline stage that slowed it down, and adding the metric that catches it next time. The next day you might pair with an applied scientist to backtest a candidate detection against retained telemetry before it ships, then pick up an operational ticket and automate away its root cause so no one handles it again. You will obsess over the two latencies that define the platform, the time from event to detection and the time from detection to containment action, and treat every manual step you find as a candidate for deletion. The team is new, so what you build now becomes the foundation others build on.
About The Team
Leo Space Security protects the people, facilities, hardware, and supply chain behind a global satellite constellation. The Engineering and R\&D team within this organization builds the platforms and tooling the security pillar teams operate on, moving security operations from manual triage to correlation-based detection, automated response, and agentic AI. The team is composed of applied scientists, software engineers, and security engineers working across physical and digital security domains.

#### Training & Career Growth
We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.
#### Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve.

As a Security Engineer III on the Government & Public Services team, you will be responsible for...
The Splunk Detection Engineer is responsible for designing, developing, tuning, and maintaining Splunk-based detection content that enables SOC analysts to identify, investigate, and respond to cybersecurity threats. This role focuses on converting threat intelligence, incident lessons learned, and operational requirements into actionable correlation searches, alerts, investigations, dashboards, and response workflows across IT, IoT, and OT environments.
The engineer partners closely with SOC analysts, incident responders, threat hunters, and infrastructure teams to improve detection fidelity, reduce false positives, document analyst response procedures, and continuously enhance the SOC's detection capability.

Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
Effective written and verbal communication skills
Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
Ability to lead projects or workstreams
Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
Ability to meet deadlines
Ability to mentor and provide clear guidance to others
The team
Deloitte's Government & Public Services (GPS) practice - our people, ideas, technology and outcomes - is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise.
Our Cyber Defense & Resilience offering assists clients in defending against advanced threats by transforming security operations, monitoring technology, data analytics, and threat intelligence. Helps manage and protect dynamic attack surfaces and provides rapid crisis and cyber incident response, ensuring clients can be ready for, respond to, and recover from business disruptions.

Required:
Bachelor's Degree required.
Active Secret Clearance required.
Ability to work onsite in Herndon, VA up to 3 days a week.
2+ years of experience within the following:
Hands-on experience developing and managing production Splunk detection content in a SOC environment.
Strong proficiency with Splunk SPL.
Experience creating and maintaining Splunk Enterprise Security correlation searches, notable events, or risk-based alerts.
Experience designing actionable detections and tuning alerts to reduce false positives.
Experience creating scheduled and ad hoc searches, dashboards, reports, and investigative queries.
Experience with intrusion, detection, and incident response in a SOC environment.
Knowledge of Splunk CIM, data models, event types, tags, field extractions, and severity criteria.
Experience with Windows and Linux security telemetry and event collection.
Ability to test, troubleshoot, document, and maintain detection content throughout its lifecycle.
Ability to travel 15%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
